title: Health-insurer concentration links market power and adverse selection to premiums, plan design, and consumer welfare
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34928, Competition in Health Insurance Markets
geography: United States; commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid health-insurance markets

denominator.unit: market segments examined: commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid

concentration.value: US health-insurance markets are highly concentrated and becoming more concentrated over time

coverage_scope.value: The paper documents concentration across commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid markets

consumer_path.value: Market structure can shape premiums, plan design, and consumer welfare through competition and information conditions

observations.method: Review and empirical analysis of competition, concentration, asymmetric information, premiums, plan design, and consumer-welfare mechanisms across major US insurance segments.
observations.uncertainty: The abstract does not disclose every concentration measure, market-year observation, estimate, or subgroup result; concentration alone does not identify the welfare effect for a particular enrollee.
observations.subgroup: Consumers in commercial insurance, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid markets, with different health risks, information, subsidies, provider networks, and switching options.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some concentration may reflect scale economies, network breadth, risk pooling, or administrative efficiencies; a structural measure is not automatically evidence of harmful conduct.

observations.period: 2026 paper; asymmetric information and plan-market outcomes

information_mechanism.value: Asymmetric information, particularly adverse selection, interacts with market power

premium_plan_link.value: The interaction shapes premiums and plan design

welfare_boundary.value: Consumer welfare depends on both competition and information/risk conditions

observations.method: Economic analysis combining market-structure evidence with adverse-selection and consumer-welfare mechanisms.
observations.uncertainty: Adverse selection is not directly observed for every enrollee in the abstract, and plan design can affect access, quality, provider choice, and out-of-pocket cost in different directions.
observations.subgroup: Higher- and lower-risk enrollees, informed and less-informed consumers, subsidized and unsubsidized purchasers, and consumers with different ability to switch plans.
observations.counterinterpretation: A plan with a higher premium may offer broader coverage or lower cost sharing; apparent consumer harm cannot be inferred from premiums without plan generosity, network, utilization, and enrollee-risk measures.

observations.period: 2026 paper; insurer consolidation and policy response

denominator.unit: policy tools discussed: antitrust enforcement, risk adjustment, regulation, and informational interventions

consolidation_premium.value: Empirical evidence confirms that insurer consolidation raises premiums

policy_routes.value: Antitrust, risk adjustment, regulation, and information interventions are discussed as ways to shape competition and consumer welfare

implementation_gap.value: Policy design does not itself establish premium relief, better plan choice, usable switching, or improved health outcomes

observations.method: Synthesis of empirical market evidence and policy mechanisms for improving competition and consumer welfare.
observations.uncertainty: The abstract does not estimate the effect of each policy tool, distributional incidence, implementation cost, or the time needed for competition reforms to reach consumers.
observations.subgroup: Enrollees, employers, insurers, providers, regulators, and public programs with different bargaining positions and exposure to consolidation.
observations.counterinterpretation: A policy can lower premiums while narrowing networks or reducing plan stability; conversely, higher premiums may accompany more generous coverage. Remedy must track total consumer access and realized protection.

related_sources.claim: Official NBER landing page with market concentration, adverse selection, premium, plan-design, consolidation, and policy-tool findings.
NBER DOI route for the working paper.

boundary: This record adds a US health-insurance competition route linking concentration, adverse selection, premiums, plan design, consumer welfare, and policy remedies across commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid markets. It does not establish a universal concentration threshold, enrollee-level welfare effect, realized remedy, provider quality, health outcome, or household recovery.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official NBER W34928 page reviewed for the three market segments, concentration trend, adverse-selection mechanism, consolidation-premium result, and four policy-response routes.
